historical_references.reference: The ancient city of Sakhan was a significant center of learning and culture in the Islamic world during the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 CE). It was renowned for its madrasas, libraries, and mosques, attracting scholars and students from across the Islamic world.
Sakhan was also known as the 'City of a Thousand Mosques' during the Seljuq Empire (1037-1194 CE), reflecting its religious significance and the architectural splendor of its mosques.
